h1: Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL — the closest hotel to BNH Hospital, on the same street
intro: If you need to be at BNH Hospital on Convent Road and want a place you can walk to at any hour — Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL is the most direct answer · the hotel sits at no. 3 Convent Road, the same street as BNH (at no. 9/1), about 250 metres apart — a 3-minute walk along a shaded pavement · PCL designed the property as a classic boutique hotel: 55 rooms dressed in warm teak furniture, an outdoor pool, and a Thai restaurant called Glom Glorm · BTS Sala Daeng is about 7 minutes on foot and MRT Silom about 9 minutes, opening up the city for days you aren't at the hospital · rooms from about THB 1,600/night · for medical visitors, it's the simplest choice for proximity; for other travellers, it's a quiet, characterful address right in the heart of Bangkok's Silom district.

body.html: Who Le Siam Hotel Silom is for — the hotel's strongest single argument is geography: it sits on the same street as BNH Hospital, no. 3 Convent Road to the hospital's no. 9/1, about 250 metres apart · walk out the hotel door, turn right, follow the tree-lined pavement for roughly three minutes and you're at BNH's main entrance · for patients arriving for multi-day treatment, companions who want to stay close, or anyone with early-morning appointments, that kind of short, walkable distance at any hour removes a lot of friction that other neighbourhood hotels can't avoid · real guest reviews consistently reflect this: proximity to BNH is the number-one reason people choose Le Siam Hotel Silom, followed closely by praise for the staff and the convenience of the wider Silom location on days away from the hospital · that said, this isn't just a medical-visitor hotel — it's a straightforward 3-star boutique property in one of Bangkok's most accessible business districts, useful for any traveller who wants a quiet street address near the BTS and MRT network

Location and getting around — Le Siam Hotel Silom is at 3 Convent Road, Silom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500 · Convent Road is a quieter residential-commercial soi that runs off the main Silom corridor, lined with trees and a few embassies · for rail travel, BTS Sala Daeng is about a 7-minute walk and MRT Silom is about 9 minutes, giving you two lines and quick access to Siam, Asok, Sukhumvit, Yaowarat, or Hua Lamphong without touching traffic · Lumpini Park, Bangkok's central green lung, is about 7 minutes on foot — useful for an early walk or run · the Patpong night market and Silom Road's restaurant strip are a 5-minute stroll · Suvarnabhumi Airport is roughly 30-45 minutes by car; the hotel arranges airport transfers · one small note from reviews: the walk to BTS or MRT involves some narrow pavement sections that can feel warm midday, so a quick Grab is always an option for those who'd rather not walk in the heat
"Very good location, just behind park silom building. Just 5 mins from BTS. Hotel is a bit outdated but well kept and clean. Staff are friendly and helpful."

Rooms and decor — Le Siam Hotel Silom has 55 air-conditioned rooms across five types · the entry level is the Classic Queen Room, then the Deluxe Twin Room for two beds, stepping up to the One Bedroom Suite at around 43 sqm with a separate living area — particularly practical if a companion needs their own space — and the largest is the Le Siam Suite at around 65 sqm with a sitting room, dining area, and work space · all rooms feature Tempur-Pedic beds, a 40-inch LED TV, a minibar, a safe, in-room bottled water, and free Wi-Fi · the design language is warm and traditional, built around dark teak furniture against cream walls — unpretentious and easy to be in for extended stays · what reviews say consistently: rooms feel generous for the price, the beds are comfortable, and the air-conditioning is powerful · the honest other side: the building has age and it shows · some guests flag dated fixtures, signs of wear on furniture, musty smells in certain rooms, and the occasional maintenance issue in bathrooms (dripping taps, thermostat-resistant air-con) · checking the room on arrival and flagging any issue immediately is the clearest advice from experienced guests here

Facilities and pool — for a 55-room mid-range property in central Bangkok, Le Siam Hotel Silom offers a solid complement of amenities · the main draw beyond the location is the outdoor swimming pool with a separate children's pool — a genuine bonus in this price range in central Silom, and one that reviews mention warmly as a place to decompress after a hospital visit or a long day · beside the pool there's a small library, a quiet reading-and-working space · restaurant Glom Glorm Thai Eatery handles breakfast (buffet, THB 390 per person, 06:30-10:30) and Thai dining through the day · the hotel also has a conference room for business, concierge, dry-cleaning, 24-hour front desk, and luggage storage · one flag raised in several TripAdvisor reviews: the pool ladder is steep with no supplementary grab bar, which can be difficult for older guests or anyone with limited mobility — a real consideration if you're accompanying a patient

Food and service — Glom Glorm's Thai menu earns generally positive marks; the food quality sits comfortably above what you'd expect at budget hotels nearby · breakfast reviews are more mixed: some guests find it adequate and fresh, while others describe the selection as limited and note that hot dishes are sometimes served lukewarm · the surrounding neighbourhood is rich enough in street food and local restaurants that many guests skip the in-house breakfast in favour of exploring, which is easy from this location · on service, this is where the hotel consistently wins in reviews: staff are described as genuinely warm, attentive, and notably helpful for guests navigating a hospital stay — people mention the front desk proactively helping with transport logistics to BNH, or keeping an eye on arrival times for medical appointments · 24-hour reception is standard and valued highly by medical visitors · a minor note: a handful of reviews mention that English communication among some staff members can be limited, though the team generally manages well with international guests

"Excellent value for money, nice big room for the price. The location is great — walking distance to Sala Daeng BTS and everything in Silom. The staff were genuinely kind and helped me figure out bus routes to the hospital every morning."

What real guests say (good and less good) — drawing from Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and other platforms, the picture is consistent · On the plus side: an outstanding location — walking distance to both BNH Hospital and the BTS/MRT network, spacious rooms for the price, warm teak decor that feels characterful rather than generic, genuinely kind staff who go out of their way for guests managing medical visits, the outdoor pool and children's pool as a welcome bonus, and strong value per baht · On the watch-out side: the most-repeated issue is the age of the building — worn furniture and fittings, some rooms with musty smells or air-conditioning that runs cold with no middle gear, occasional bathroom maintenance problems (reported dripping taps or loose fittings), a steep pool ladder without extra handrails, breakfast that repeats itself and can arrive lukewarm, and occasionally a faint smell of pest-control chemicals · the composite score of 8.8 on Trip.com (276 reviews) and 4.1/5 on TripAdvisor (524 reviews) reflects a genuinely well-liked hotel where the location and staff earn strong ratings and compensate for the physical imperfections of an older building

Rates and value — Classic Queen Rooms start from about THB 1,600/night in regular periods, rising to around THB 2,000-2,500 in high season or long weekends · Deluxe Twin Room runs roughly THB 1,800-2,200 · One Bedroom Suite around THB 2,500-3,000 · Le Siam Suite from roughly THB 3,500 · at this level of pricing, for a Convent Road address within a 3-minute walk of BNH, the value case is clear for medical visitors: no other hotel in the Silom area sits this close to the hospital's entrance · for general travellers, you're paying for location and a generous room footprint, and making peace with a property that isn't newly renovated · comparable 4-star hotels in this part of Silom typically cost 30-50% more for a similar room size · compare rates across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking, as prices can vary meaningfully between platforms on the same dates

Practical tips before you book — for guests coming for BNH: check the room as soon as you arrive and report any issue with smell, air-conditioning, or bathroom fittings before unpacking · the front desk 24-hour service means any problem can be addressed immediately, and reviews suggest staff are responsive · if you're accompanying an elderly patient, ask specifically about the pool ladder and access before assuming the pool is usable · breakfast at THB 390 extra is a reasonable add-on for a one- or two-night stay, though on longer visits the nearby neighbourhood offers more variety · always choose a free-cancellation rate if your treatment schedule is uncertain · and compare prices across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com — all three carry this property and rates can differ by date and lead time

highlights.title: Closest to BNH — 3-min walk
highlights.text: Located on the same Convent Road as BNH Hospital, roughly 250 metres apart. Walk out the door and you're there in about 3 minutes — no ride needed at any hour.

highlights.title: BTS Sala Daeng ~7 min · MRT Silom ~9 min
highlights.text: Two rail lines within easy walking distance. Reach Siam, Asok, Sukhumvit, or link to the MRT toward Yaowarat without touching Bangkok's traffic.

highlights.title: Outdoor pool with children's pool
highlights.text: An outdoor pool plus a children's pool — genuinely uncommon at this price in central Silom. A good spot to unwind between hospital visits or after a day in the city.

honestSummary: Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL earns its place on any BNH Hospital shortlist for one overriding reason: it's on the same street, 3 minutes on foot, closer than any other hotel in the area · staff are a genuine strong point, rooms are spacious for the price, and having a pool in this location is a real bonus · the trade-off is an older building with some rooms that show wear — this is a hotel you choose for its address and its people, not for gleaming newness.
honestChecks: If you're staying for BNH treatment over several days — this is the closest hotel and the 3-min walk at any hour is its main value · check the room on arrival; flag anything with smell, air-con, or bathroom straight away and staff will help

If you or a patient has limited mobility and needs pool access — the pool ladder is steep and lacks supplementary grab bars · ask the hotel about this before assuming the pool is accessible, or skip the pool and use the hotel's other quiet spaces
If you need a freshly renovated, spotless property — the building has age and occasional wear shows · newer options exist in Silom and Sathorn, though they cost more and are further from BNH

tips.title: Walking route to BNH Hospital
tips.body: Turn right out of the hotel, follow Convent Road for about 250 metres — BNH's main entrance will be on your left. It's shaded most of the way and takes roughly 3 minutes at a normal pace.

tips.title: Check the room on arrival
tips.body: Test the air-con, check for any musty smell, and look over the bathroom before unpacking. Staff are available 24 hours and, based on reviews, are willing to fix issues or move you to a better room.

tips.title: Use BTS or MRT instead of taxis in rush hour
tips.body: BTS Sala Daeng (~7 min walk) and MRT Silom (~9 min) connect you to most of Bangkok faster than a cab at peak times. Lumpini Park is also in easy walking range for a morning walk.

tips.title: Book free cancellation if your schedule is uncertain
tips.body: Medical trip plans can change. Choose a free-cancellation rate and compare prices across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com — there can be a meaningful difference between platforms on the same dates.

faqTitle: FAQ — Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL

faq.q: How far is Le Siam Hotel Silom from BNH Hospital?
faq.a: Le Siam Hotel Silom by PCL is at 3 Convent Road and BNH Hospital is at 9/1 Convent Road — on the same street, approximately 250 metres apart, roughly a 3-minute walk along a shaded pavement. No taxi or ride is needed.

faq.q: How far is Le Siam Hotel Silom from BTS Sala Daeng?
faq.a: BTS Sala Daeng is about a 7-minute walk from the hotel · MRT Silom station is approximately 9 minutes on foot · both stations connect you quickly to Siam, Asok, Sukhumvit, Yaowarat, and Hua Lamphong.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Le Siam Hotel Silom?
faq.a: Rooms start from about THB 1,600/night for a Classic Queen Room · Deluxe Twin Room around THB 1,800 · One Bedroom Suite (~43 sqm) around THB 2,500 · Le Siam Suite (~65 sqm) from around THB 3,500 · rates vary by season and platform — compare Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Le Siam Hotel Silom have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — there's an outdoor swimming pool with a children's pool · breakfast is a buffet at THB 390 per person, served 06:30-10:30 at Glom Glorm Thai Eatery · reviews describe breakfast as adequate but limited in variety, so guests staying multiple nights often explore the neighbourhood's street food and cafes too.

faq.q: Is Le Siam Hotel Silom suitable for a medical stay at BNH Hospital?
faq.a: It's very well suited to medical stays on the distance front — a 3-minute walk at any hour of the day or night · 24-hour reception is a real advantage for guests with unpredictable schedules · the One Bedroom Suite works well if a companion needs a separate sleeping space · one note: the pool ladder is steep and lacks supplementary grab bars, which may make the pool difficult for guests with limited mobility.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Le Siam Hotel Silom old?
faq.a: The building has age and reviews reflect this — some rooms show worn furniture, and a few guests report musty smells or minor bathroom maintenance issues · the practical advice from experienced reviewers: check the room on arrival and ask for a different one if you're not satisfied · overall the hotel is clean and comfortable, but it isn't a newly renovated property.
